correctness.rationale: For a correlated standard-normal adjacent pair, direct integration gives \(\mathbb E[Z_0^2\mathbf 1\{Z_0Z_1<0\}]=\mathbb P(Z_0Z_1<0)-\rho\sqrt{1-\rho^2}/\pi\). Restoring scale gives the local endpoint covariance. The stationary Gaussian AR(1) Markov property propagates centered squares geometrically away from either endpoint, so every edge-to-site covariance is the displayed local factor times \((\rho^2)^d\). Summing this finite kernel proves the closed formula and its opposite-sign law. The packaged checker performs 7 numerical integral checks, 632 closed-form versus unsimplified edge-sum checks, and 731 sign/independence checks.

value.rationale: Zero-crossing count and total quadratic energy are canonical complementary summaries of a Gaussian time series. The result gives an exact finite-sample dependence law and a geometric local mechanism: positive serial correlation makes a crossing negatively associated with squared amplitude at every site, negative serial correlation reverses the association, and independence is the exact zero boundary. This is structurally stronger than a one-number computation and directly contrasts with the even-in-\(\rho\) zero-crossing variance documented in the closest AR(1) source.
